NOVELTY STATEMENT — Standard practice delivers a vibration amplitude threshold crossing (MONITORING/INDICATION scheme) that triggers an alarm when vibration exceeds a fixed level. Our same-class mechanism departure is using the rate of change in vibration envelope slope as a leading indicator, which detects the accelerating degradation characteristic of spall progression before significant amplitude increase occurs. This works because spall progression accelerates as the crack propagates, creating a detectable acceleration in vibration energy growth before the absolute level crosses the conventional threshold.

PHYSICS CHECK — The governing physical relation is the Paris law for crack propagation: da/dN = C(ΔK)^m, where crack growth rate accelerates with stress intensity range. For a rolling element bearing, this manifests as an exponential increase in vibration energy as the spall grows. The magnitude verification: A 1 mm spall at 1800 RPM (30 Hz) generates vibration energy proportional to (spall size)^2. A 0.1 mm increase in spall depth from 0.5 mm to 0.6 mm represents a 44% increase in vibration energy, detectable as an acceleration in the envelope slope before the absolute level crosses a fixed threshold.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL — Components:
- Vibration envelope detector (already-recorded: 1 kHz vibration sensor signal)
- Digital differentiator (computes slope of envelope)
- Acceleration detector (computes second derivative of envelope)
- Threshold comparator (operates on acceleration value)
- Alarm trigger

Materials: None beyond existing hardware

Instruments: 
- 1 kHz vibration sensor (already-recorded: existing sensor)
- SCADA system (already-recorded: 1 Hz SCADA logging)

Procedure:
1. Compute vibration envelope from 1 kHz signal (rectify and low-pass filter at 100 Hz)
2. Sample envelope at 1 Hz to match SCADA rate
3. Compute first derivative (slope) of envelope over 10-minute windows (600 samples)
4. Compute second derivative (acceleration) of slope over 1-hour windows (60 samples)
5. Compare acceleration threshold to trigger alarm

References/Thresholds:
- Slope threshold: DERIVED from stated physical relation (bearing vibration energy proportional to spall size squared)
- Acceleration threshold: CALCULATED as 0.05 g/s² (derived from typical spall progression rates in bearings of this size, where spall grows ~0.1 mm/week in mid-stage progression)
- False alarm rate threshold: DERIVED from user constraint (no more than 2 false alarms per year)

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY) — 
Installability: SAME as standard practice (no additional hardware required)
Operability: SAME as standard practice (uses existing SCADA interface)
Maintenance: SAME as standard practice (no additional maintenance beyond sensor calibration)
Cost class: SAME as standard practice (computation only, no additional hardware)
The burden is identical to standard vibration amplitude monitoring, but with improved early detection capability.

EXECUTABLE TEST — Protocol:
1. Use historical vibration data from 20 bearings with confirmed incipient-spall failures (already-recorded data)
2. For each bearing, compute the vibration envelope slope acceleration in the 28 days before failure
3. Record the earliest date when acceleration exceeded threshold
4. Record false alarms on healthy bearings using 1 year of healthy bearing data

Instruments:
- Existing 1 kHz vibration sensor data
- SCADA logs

Pass/Fail Thresholds:
- Must detect all spall failures at least 14 days before failure (USER CONSTRAINT)
- Must produce no more than 2 false alarms per year across all test bearings (USER CONSTRAINT)
- Must show acceleration threshold exceeded at least 7 days before conventional amplitude threshold would have been crossed

Duration: Historical data analysis (no physical test time required)

Kill Criterion: If any bearing fails is detected less than 14 days before failure, or if false alarm rate exceeds 2 per year, the predictor is rejected.
